item.research_question: Can high-entropy alloys be designed to simultaneously achieve high Snoek-type damping capacity, high mechanical strength, and high ductility at elevated temperatures?
item.material_system: Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi base HEA, (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi)98O2 (O-2 HEA), and (Ta0.5Nb0.5HfZrTi)98N2 (N-2 HEA)
item.processing_route: Arc-melting of pure metals (purity >99.9 wt%), TiN (99.9 wt%), and TiO2 (99.9 wt%) in a Ti-gettered high-purity argon atmosphere; remelted at least eight times; drop-cast into a water-cooled copper mold (10 mm × 10 mm × 60 mm)
item.test_conditions: Damping measured via multifunction internal friction apparatus at 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 4.0 Hz, temperature range 300–1100 K, heating rate 2 K min⁻¹, max strain amplitude 2 × 10⁻⁴; Tensile tests at room temperature, strain rate 1 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹
key_findings: The O-2 HEA achieved a peak damping capacity (tanδ_max) of 0.020 at 1.0 Hz, while the N-2 HEA reached 0.027 at 1.0 Hz.
The N-2 HEA exhibited a yield strength of 1362 MPa and elongation of ~11.9%, while the O-2 HEA showed 1138 MPa yield strength and ~20% elongation.
The peak damping temperature (T_p) for the HEAs was approximately 730–747 K at 1.0 Hz, roughly 100 K higher than traditional Snoek-type alloys.
Activation energies (H) were determined to be 2.06 eV (base), 2.40 eV (O-2), and 4.06 eV (N-2).
Approximately 18.5% of oxygen atoms in the O-2 HEA formed ordered oxygen complexes, whereas only ~5.3% of nitrogen atoms in the N-2 HEA formed ordered nitrogen complexes.
The base HEA showed a yield strength of ~810 MPa and elongation of ~10.8%, which increased significantly upon interstitial doping.
The damping peaks were asymmetrically broadened, indicating a variety of local atomic configurations affecting interstitial site switching.
item.mechanism: High damping arises from stress-induced reorientation of interstitial atoms (Snoek relaxation) within severely distorted bcc lattices; high strength and ductility result from solid-solution strengthening and the formation of ordered interstitial complexes (OOCs/ONCs) that impede dislocation motion and enhance strain hardening.
item.limitations: The text notes that the complexity of the alloy composition makes complete peak deconvolution analysis difficult, and the specific clusters attributing to certain peaks in the base HEA could not be determined due to complicated element occupation.
item.future_work: The authors state that the alloy design strategy could be used to develop other high-damping HEAs and suggest potential applications in the automotive and aerospace industries.
quotes: The current HEAs exhibit good damping features with tanδ max > 0.01.
The addition of oxygen or nitrogen effectively further enhances the damping capacity.
The interstitial doped HEAs retain the same level of ductility but display 70 to 105% higher yield strength than Ti-25Nb-1.5O alloy.
